summary: CCC-built lookout dedicated in October 1938 on the US-Mexico border; last staffing found is 1965; demolished after 1975; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Enclosed battered timber tower about 20 ft tall with a 14x14 ft wood cab; likely a National Park Service Plan 7 design
facts.status_note: Demolished sometime after 1975 per the Former Fire Lookout Sites register and the FFLA page; the Descanso page says it no longer exists. A 2019 hiker's post records only a metal post in concrete at the summit and does not tie it to the lookout.

staffing.status: last known lookout retired in summer 1965

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CalFire)

events.note: Dedicated October 23, 1938, per a 1938 California Ranger report, after CCC crews built the road and lookout building. The FFLA page gives 1939 for construction.

Lee O. Wyatt, a California Division of Forestry lookout for 20 years with Tecate Peak as his station, retired in summer 1965 (obituary dated January 20, 1966). The sources do not say when staffing ended.
Demolished sometime after 1975; no exact year given. The year shown is the cutoff, and demolition came after it.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on April 13, 2009.

corrections.why: The 1938 California Ranger report, reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page, describes the dedication in October 1938 and the CCC work as already done. The 1939 date comes only from the FFLA page.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA page gives 1939 for construction, but the 1938 report describes a dedication on October 23, 1938 with the CCC work already done. The story gives the 1938 dedication and notes the FFLA date.
The 1938 report places the lookout northwest of Tecate. The Descanso page places it just west of Tecate, about a quarter mile inside the US. The story reports both and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Access: the record says unknown and no source states current access, so facts.access is omitted. A 2019 post (updated December 2025) says a National Defense Area may affect access; check with CalFire or the land manager before any access level is set. Coordinates: the record's 32.57961, -116.68867 matches the firelookout.org row for this site; the FFLOS page gives N 32.579350, W 116.683330, about 0.5 km away. Not changed. Register numbers: the firelookout.org row for this site lists FFLOS US 521, CA 7 and also an NHLR US 382, CA 43 line, which the NHLR California index assigns to Needles Lookout, so the record's note that the two sites share a register number is not confirmed. Elevation: the record's 929.3 m matches FFLOS (3,049 ft, 929 m); the FFLA page says 3855 ft / 1175 m. Unresolved; the story does not use elevation. Height: 6.1 m is the 20 ft in the sources converted to metres. The 1938 and 1966 items are read through the Forest Lookouts reprints; the original newspapers were not checked. A search result lists an SDG&E P25 radio site named Tecate Peak (radioreference.com/db/site/45710); I did not open it, so the story does not claim any radio facility stands there today.
